What to look for

This is issue 4708's shader: a class template with two NON-member (namespace scope)
operator+ templates, used as `arr1 + 2.0f`. The result is stored to a UAV so that a
compiler which accepts the program shows its work; in the reporter's original the result
was unused and an accepting compiler would emit an empty entry point, which reads as
"nothing happened".

Compare the panes:

- Both DXC panes fail. The older one rejects only the USE of the operator; the trunk one
  additionally rejects each DECLARATION, a diagnostic added in 2023. Same outcome, better
  wording.
- The Clang HLSL pane succeeds and emits a resource binding for the UAV plus a single
  buffer store. Read the float constant in that store: it is the sum the free operator
  computes, folded at compile time. So the operator was found, called and evaluated -- the
  pane is not merely silent.

Compiler Explorer builds DXC in Release and appends debug-info flags to its DXC panes;
neither affects this comparison, which is a front-end accept/reject question. dxc_trunk is
a rolling build, so treat its exact wording as current rather than pinned.
